answer: We define a system where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds enforce capital barriers, such that any node at a given network vertex incurs a staking collateral requirement scaling quadratically with identity replication. By embedding a subgame-perfect punishment matrix, the mechanism triggers slashing penalties upon proof of collateral overlap, ensuring the expected utility of a Sybil plume is strictly negative. This equilibrium forces agents to meadow in singular, high-value nodes, yielding a robust Nash equilibrium.
